verifications.claim: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the crewed Artemis II mission, according to NASA (.gov) and SpaceNews.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'for a launch as soon as April 1'; R8: 'No Earlier Than April 1'; R9/R10: 'as early as April 1'; 'launch attempt Wednesday, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple NASA (.gov) sources and SpaceNews directly state or confirm targeting April 1 for Artemis II launch.

verifications.claim: Daily launch windows for the Artemis II mission are available through April 6, 2026, according to NASA (.gov) and SpaceNews.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'NASA has two-hour launch windows available daily between April 1 and 6'; R2: 'April 2-6'; R5: 'must launch Artemis 2 by April 6'
verifications.reasoning: SpaceNews directly supports daily windows through April 6 attributed to NASA; NASA (.gov) refs imply April targeting but not explicitly daily windows, supported overall.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket has returned to Pad 39B for final preparations for the 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon, according to Florida Today and Spaceflight Now.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA's giant moon rocket is back on the launch pad... for what appears to be an imminent launch... 10-day journey around the moon'; R4: 'returned to the launch pad... Launch Pad 39B... about 10 days after liftoff'
verifications.reasoning: Florida Today (R2) and Spaceflight Now (R4) directly confirm SLS return to Pad 39B for Artemis II 10-day lunar mission preparations.

verifications.claim: NASA (.gov) says the target launch date for Artemis II is April 1, 2026 (No Earlier Than).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R8: 'No Earlier Than April 1'; R10: 'as early as Wednesday, April 1'; 'NET April 1'
verifications.reasoning: NASA (.gov) sources explicitly state target launch no earlier than April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: NASA (.gov) says launch opportunities for Artemis II extend through April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: NASA (.gov) refs (R8, R9, R10) mention NET/target April 1 but do not specify opportunities extending through April 6.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews notes the next opportunity for Artemis II is April 30, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'After April 6, the next launch opportunity is April 30'
verifications.reasoning: SpaceNews (R6) directly states next opportunity after April 6 is April 30.

verifications.claim: NASA (.gov) says the launch site for Artemis II is Kennedy Space Center, Florida (Pad 39B).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: 'Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center'; R10: 'Launch Pad 39B at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: NASA (.gov) sources explicitly name Kennedy Space Center Pad 39B as Artemis II launch site.

verifications.claim: NASA (.gov) reports the Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day flight crewed by four astronauts to test Orion spacecraft systems around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R8: 'Four astronauts will venture around the Moon... The 10-day flight will help confirm systems and hardware'; R9/R10: '10-day mission around the Moon... first crewed flight... test systems'
verifications.reasoning: NASA (.gov) confirms 10-day crewed flight around Moon to verify/test Orion/SLS systems; phrasing closely matches.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, according to the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: KSC Visitor Complex sources (R1, R3) list exact crew names.

verifications.claim: The rocket and Orion capsule were transported back to the launch pad around March 20, 2026, following final checkouts, according to NASA (.gov) and Florida Today.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'rolled... back to the launch pad around 12:20 a.m. ET Friday, March 20'; R9: 'began rolling to Launch Pad 39B... March 20'; R10: 'arrived at Launch Pad 39B... March 20... following... repairs [checkouts]'
verifications.reasoning: Florida Today (R2) and NASA (.gov) (R9, R10) confirm transport back to pad around March 20 after VAB repairs/checkouts.
